nodes.name: Limits and Continuity
nodes.description: The limit formalising the value a function approaches near a point, made rigorous by the epsilon-delta definition, with continuity meaning the limit equals the function value.
nodes.visual_hint: Plot f(x) with a draggable point approaching a; show the limit value as the point nears a from both sides.

evidence_refs.locator: Course unit/session index: Differentiation

nodes.name: Definition of Derivative
nodes.description: The derivative defined as the limit of difference quotients, giving the instantaneous rate of change and the slope of the tangent line to a curve.
nodes.visual_hint: Slider for h: draw the secant through (x,f(x)) and (x+h,f(x+h)) collapsing to the tangent as h→0.

evidence_refs.locator: Course unit/session index: Differentiation

nodes.name: Differentiation Rules
nodes.description: Rules for differentiating combinations of functions, including the power, product, and quotient rules, enabling derivatives without returning to the limit definition.

evidence_refs.locator: Course unit/session index: Differentiation

nodes.name: Chain Rule
nodes.description: The chain rule differentiating a composite function as the derivative of the outer function times the derivative of the inner function.

evidence_refs.locator: Course unit/session index: Differentiation Techniques and Related Rates

nodes.name: Implicit Differentiation
nodes.description: Implicit differentiation finding derivatives of relations not solved for one variable by differentiating both sides and solving for the derivative.
nodes.visual_hint: Plot an implicit relation (e.g. x²+y²=25) and show the tangent slope at a draggable point on the curve.

evidence_refs.locator: Course unit/session index: Differentiation Techniques and Related Rates

nodes.name: Related Rates
nodes.description: Related-rates problems linking the time derivatives of related quantities through an equation, solving for one unknown rate given the others.

evidence_refs.locator: Course unit/session index: Differentiation Techniques and Related Rates

nodes.name: Linear Approximation
nodes.description: Linear approximation using the tangent line to estimate function values near a point, the basis of differentials and Newton's method.
nodes.visual_hint: Plot f(x) and its tangent line at a; slider for x comparing the true value against the linear approximation.

evidence_refs.locator: Course unit/session index: Applications of Differentiation

nodes.name: Curve Sketching
nodes.description: Using first and second derivatives to locate extrema, intervals of increase and decrease, concavity, and inflection points to sketch a curve.
nodes.visual_hint: Plot f(x) with toggles for f′ and f″; mark extrema, inflection points, and increase/decrease intervals.

evidence_refs.locator: Course unit/session index: Applications of Differentiation

nodes.name: Mean Value Theorem
nodes.description: The mean value theorem guaranteeing a point where the instantaneous rate of change equals the average rate over an interval, with key consequences.
nodes.visual_hint: Plot f on [a,b] with the secant line and a draggable point c where the tangent is parallel to the secant.

evidence_refs.locator: Course unit/session index: Applications of Differentiation

nodes.name: Riemann Sums
nodes.description: Riemann sums approximating the area under a curve by summing the areas of rectangles, whose limit defines the definite integral.
nodes.visual_hint: Slider for rectangle count n; draw left/right/midpoint Riemann rectangles under f(x) and show the sum approaching the area.

evidence_refs.locator: Course unit/session index: Riemann Sums and Definite Integrals

nodes.name: Definite Integrals
nodes.description: The definite integral defined as the limit of Riemann sums, giving the signed area under a curve, with linearity and additivity properties.
nodes.visual_hint: Shade signed area under f(x) between draggable bounds a,b; colour positive/negative regions and show the integral value.

evidence_refs.locator: Course unit/session index: Riemann Sums and Definite Integrals

nodes.name: Fundamental Theorem of Calculus
nodes.description: The fundamental theorem of calculus linking differentiation and integration, evaluating definite integrals via antiderivatives and differentiating integral functions.
nodes.visual_hint: Animate the accumulation function A(x)=∫ₐˣ f as x moves, showing A′(x)=f(x).

evidence_refs.locator: Course unit/session index: Fundamental Theorem of Calculus and Integration by Substitution

nodes.name: Integration by Substitution
nodes.description: Integration by substitution reversing the chain rule by changing variables to transform an integral into a simpler, recognisable form.

evidence_refs.locator: Course unit/session index: Fundamental Theorem of Calculus and Integration by Substitution

nodes.name: Integration by Parts
nodes.description: Integration by parts reversing the product rule to integrate products of functions, trading one integral for an often simpler one.

evidence_refs.locator: Course unit/session index: Techniques of Integration

nodes.name: Trigonometric Integrals
nodes.description: Techniques for integrating products and powers of trigonometric functions using identities to reduce them to directly integrable forms.

evidence_refs.locator: Course unit/session index: Techniques of Integration

nodes.name: Trigonometric Substitution
nodes.description: Trigonometric substitution evaluating integrals containing quadratic radicals by substituting trigonometric functions and applying identities.

evidence_refs.locator: Course unit/session index: Techniques of Integration

nodes.name: Partial Fractions
nodes.description: Partial-fraction decomposition rewriting a rational function as a sum of simpler fractions that can be integrated term by term.

evidence_refs.locator: Course unit/session index: Integration Techniques and Area

nodes.name: Improper Integrals
nodes.description: Improper integrals defined by limits, evaluating integrals over infinite intervals or with unbounded integrands and testing for convergence.
nodes.visual_hint: Plot f(x) with the upper bound b→∞; show the accumulating area and whether it converges to a finite value.

evidence_refs.locator: Course unit/session index: Integration Techniques and Area

nodes.name: Area Between Curves
nodes.description: Computing the area between two curves by integrating the difference of their functions over the interval where they bound a region.
nodes.visual_hint: Shade the region between two draggable curves over [a,b] and show the integral of their difference.

evidence_refs.locator: Course unit/session index: Integration Techniques and Area

nodes.name: Volumes of Solids
nodes.description: Computing volumes of solids of revolution and general solids using slicing, disk, washer, and cylindrical-shell integration methods.
nodes.visual_hint: Rotate a region about an axis into a solid; slider sweeps a disk/washer cross-section and shows the volume integral.

evidence_refs.locator: Course unit/session index: Applications of Integration

nodes.name: Arc Length
nodes.description: Computing the length of a plane curve by integrating the arc-length element derived from the Pythagorean relationship of differentials.
nodes.visual_hint: Approximate a curve's length with a slider for the number of straight segments converging to the arc-length integral.

evidence_refs.locator: Course unit/session index: Applications of Integration

nodes.name: Work
nodes.description: Computing physical work done by a variable force by integrating force over displacement, applied to springs, pumping, and lifting problems.

evidence_refs.locator: Course unit/session index: Applications of Integration

nodes.name: Sequences and Series
nodes.description: Sequences as ordered lists of numbers and series as their sums, with convergence describing whether they approach a finite limit.
nodes.visual_hint: Plot sequence terms and their partial sums against n to show convergence or divergence.

evidence_refs.locator: Course unit/session index: Sequences and Series and Convergence Tests

nodes.name: Convergence Tests
nodes.description: Tests for series convergence, including the integral, comparison, ratio, and root tests, determining whether an infinite series sums to a finite value.
nodes.visual_hint: Decision-tree diagram choosing a convergence test (integral / comparison / ratio / root) from the series' form.

evidence_refs.locator: Course unit/session index: Sequences and Series and Convergence Tests

nodes.name: Power Series
nodes.description: Power series representing functions as infinite polynomials, with a radius and interval of convergence determining where they converge.
nodes.visual_hint: Plot a function against its power-series partial sums; slider for term count and shade the interval of convergence.

evidence_refs.locator: Course unit/session index: Power Series and Taylor Series

nodes.name: Taylor Series
nodes.description: Taylor and Maclaurin series expanding a function as a power series about a point using its derivatives, approximating functions locally.
nodes.visual_hint: Plot f(x) and its Taylor polynomial about a; slider for degree n to watch it hug the curve.

evidence_refs.locator: Course unit/session index: Power Series and Taylor Series

nodes.name: Dot Product
nodes.description: Vectors with magnitude and direction, and the dot product measuring projection and the angle between them, yielding a scalar from two vectors.
nodes.visual_hint: Drag two vectors; show the dot product, the projection of one onto the other, and the angle between them.

evidence_refs.locator: Course unit/session index: Dot Product and Cross Product

nodes.name: Cross Product
nodes.description: The cross product of two vectors producing a vector perpendicular to both, whose magnitude equals the area of the parallelogram they span.
nodes.visual_hint: Drag two 3D vectors; show the perpendicular cross-product vector and the parallelogram area its magnitude measures.

evidence_refs.locator: Course unit/session index: Dot Product and Cross Product

nodes.name: Lines and Planes
nodes.description: Equations of lines and planes in three-dimensional space using points, direction vectors, and normal vectors in vector and scalar forms.
nodes.visual_hint: Show a line or plane in 3D from a point and a direction/normal; drag to watch its equation update.

evidence_refs.locator: Course unit/session index: Lines and Planes and Parametric Curves

nodes.name: Parametric Curves
nodes.description: Vector-valued functions tracing curves in space, whose derivatives give the velocity and acceleration along the parametrised path.
nodes.visual_hint: Trace a parametric curve r(t) with a slider for t showing the position, velocity, and acceleration vectors.

evidence_refs.locator: Course unit/session index: Lines and Planes and Parametric Curves

nodes.name: Multivariable Functions
nodes.description: Functions of several variables mapping points to values, visualised through level curves and surfaces, generalising single-variable functions.
nodes.visual_hint: Show a surface z=f(x,y) with its level curves; drag to rotate and read heights off the contours.

evidence_refs.locator: Course unit/session index: Multivariable Functions and Partial Derivatives

nodes.name: Partial Derivatives
nodes.description: Partial derivatives measuring the rate of change of a multivariable function with respect to one variable while holding the others fixed.
nodes.visual_hint: Slice a surface z=f(x,y) along x and y at a point and show the two partial-derivative slopes.

evidence_refs.locator: Course unit/session index: Multivariable Functions and Partial Derivatives

nodes.name: Multivariable Chain Rule
nodes.description: The multivariable chain rule differentiating compositions of several-variable functions by summing contributions through each intermediate variable.
nodes.visual_hint: Dependency-tree diagram of the variables, showing each path's contribution in the multivariable chain rule.

evidence_refs.locator: Course unit/session index: Multivariable Chain Rule and Gradient and Directional Derivative

nodes.name: Gradient and Directional Derivative
nodes.description: The gradient vector of partial derivatives pointing in the direction of steepest increase, with directional derivatives giving rates along any direction.
nodes.visual_hint: On a contour plot show the gradient pointing to steepest increase; drag a direction to compare the directional derivative.

evidence_refs.locator: Course unit/session index: Multivariable Chain Rule and Gradient and Directional Derivative

nodes.name: Tangent Planes
nodes.description: The tangent plane approximating a surface near a point, generalising the tangent line and providing linear approximation in several variables.
nodes.visual_hint: Show the tangent plane touching a surface z=f(x,y) at a draggable point.

evidence_refs.locator: Course unit/session index: Tangent Planes and Local Extrema

nodes.name: Local Extrema
nodes.description: Finding local maxima, minima, and saddle points of multivariable functions using critical points and the second-derivative (Hessian) test.
nodes.visual_hint: Surface with maxima, minima, and saddles marked; apply the second-derivative test at a draggable critical point.

evidence_refs.locator: Course unit/session index: Tangent Planes and Local Extrema

nodes.name: Lagrange Multipliers
nodes.description: Lagrange multipliers optimising a function subject to constraints by setting its gradient proportional to the constraint gradients.
nodes.visual_hint: Contour plot with a constraint curve, showing where the objective and constraint gradients align at the optimum.

evidence_refs.locator: Course unit/session index: Lagrange Multipliers and Differentials

nodes.name: Differentials
nodes.description: Differentials approximating small changes in a multivariable function from changes in its inputs, used for linear approximation and error estimation.

evidence_refs.locator: Course unit/session index: Lagrange Multipliers and Differentials

nodes.name: Double Integrals
nodes.description: Double integrals computing volume and accumulated quantities over two-dimensional regions, evaluated as iterated single integrals.
nodes.visual_hint: Show a planar region and the volume under z=f(x,y); sweep the integration to build up the double integral.

evidence_refs.locator: Course unit/session index: Multiple Integrals

nodes.name: Polar Integrals
nodes.description: Evaluating double integrals in polar coordinates, where the area element gains a factor of r, simplifying circular and radial regions.
nodes.visual_hint: Show a polar region with the r·dr·dθ area element; sweep θ to build the polar double integral.

evidence_refs.locator: Course unit/session index: Multiple Integrals

nodes.name: Triple Integrals
nodes.description: Triple integrals computing volume and accumulated quantities over three-dimensional regions, evaluated as iterated single integrals.

evidence_refs.locator: Course unit/session index: Multiple Integrals

nodes.name: Cylindrical and Spherical Coordinates
nodes.description: Triple integration in cylindrical and spherical coordinates, with appropriate volume elements simplifying problems with axial or spherical symmetry.

evidence_refs.locator: Course unit/session index: Coordinate Changes and Vector Fields

nodes.name: Change of Variables
nodes.description: Change of variables in multiple integrals using the Jacobian determinant to account for how the transformation scales area or volume.

evidence_refs.locator: Course unit/session index: Coordinate Changes and Vector Fields

nodes.name: Vector Fields
nodes.description: Vector fields assigning a vector to each point, and line integrals accumulating a field's effect along a curve, modelling work and flow.
nodes.visual_hint: Plot a 2D vector field; drop a particle to trace its path and accumulate a line integral along a curve.

evidence_refs.locator: Course unit/session index: Coordinate Changes and Vector Fields

nodes.name: Fundamental Theorem for Line Integrals
nodes.description: The fundamental theorem for line integrals showing conservative fields have path-independent integrals computed from a potential function.
nodes.visual_hint: Diagram contrasting path-dependent integrals with path-independent ones in a conservative field.

evidence_refs.locator: Course unit/session index: Vector Calculus

nodes.name: Green's Theorem
nodes.description: Green's theorem relating a line integral around a closed plane curve to a double integral of curl over the enclosed region.
nodes.visual_hint: Show a closed curve and its enclosed region, relating the circulation line integral to the double integral of curl.

evidence_refs.locator: Course unit/session index: Vector Calculus

nodes.name: Curl and Divergence
nodes.description: Curl measuring a vector field's local rotation and divergence measuring its net outward flux per unit volume, fundamental differential operators.
nodes.visual_hint: Vector field with a paddlewheel (curl) and a source/sink box (divergence) at a draggable point.

evidence_refs.locator: Course unit/session index: Vector Calculus

nodes.name: Parametric Surfaces
nodes.description: Parametric representations of surfaces using two parameters, enabling computation of surface area through the cross product of partial derivatives.

evidence_refs.locator: Course unit/session index: Parametric Surfaces and Surface Integrals

nodes.name: Surface Integrals
nodes.description: Surface integrals accumulating a scalar field or the flux of a vector field across a surface, generalising double integrals to curved surfaces.

evidence_refs.locator: Course unit/session index: Parametric Surfaces and Surface Integrals

nodes.name: Stokes' Theorem
nodes.description: Stokes' theorem relating the line integral of a field around a closed curve to the surface integral of its curl over a bounded surface.
nodes.visual_hint: Diagram relating the boundary-curve line integral to the surface integral of curl (Stokes).

evidence_refs.locator: Course unit/session index: Stokes' Theorem and Divergence Theorem

nodes.name: Divergence Theorem
nodes.description: The divergence theorem relating the outward flux of a vector field through a closed surface to the triple integral of its divergence inside.
nodes.visual_hint: Diagram relating outward flux through a closed surface to the volume integral of divergence.

evidence_refs.locator: Course unit/session index: Stokes' Theorem and Divergence Theorem
